item.title: Prof. Prasad set to return as Deputy PM and Minister for Finance
item.description: National Federation Party Leader, Professor Biman Prasad is set to return as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in the Coalition Government after he was acquitted of the charges laid against him by FICAC. When approached by fijivillage News on Professor Prasad's acquittal and whether he would return as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said
item.content:encoded:
National Federation Party Leader, Professor Biman Prasad is set to return as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in the Coalition Government after he was acquitted of the charges laid against him by FICAC.

When approached by fijivillage News on Professor Prasad's acquittal and whether he would return as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said yes, that's what he said at the beginning.

While delivering his ruling on the no-case-to-answer submission, Magistrate Yogesh Prasad said the charges against Professor Prasad had not been proven by FICAC.

Professor Prasad is yet to receive official communication on his reappointment.

He had resigned in October last year after being charged by FICAC.

This is an interesting scenario as Prime Minister Rabuka has also said last week that any cabinet minister that votes against the Constitution Amendment Bill will his or her cabinet seat.

The National Federation Party has issued a directive to all it's MPs to vote against the Constitution Bill in the third reading in Parliament.

If they vote for the Bill, then they will lose their parliamentary seat.

item.title: Bailiff alleges Chandra's husband threatened to kill him during Navua encounter
item.description: The husband of Elaine Chandra allegedly threatened to kill a registered bailiff during an encounter at True Mart in Navua, after the bailiff attempted to serve a writ of summons on Chandra at her Pacific Harbour residence in June last year. This was revealed during the testimony of registered bailiff Mohammed Niyaz in the $1 million defamation suit brought by former Duavata News Editor Arnold Chan
item.content:encoded:
The husband of Elaine Chandra allegedly threatened to kill a registered bailiff during an encounter at True Mart in Navua, after the bailiff attempted to serve a writ of summons on Chandra at her Pacific Harbour residence in June last year.

This was revealed during the testimony of registered bailiff Mohammed Niyaz in the $1 million defamation suit brought by former Duavata News Editor Arnold Chanel against Chandra.

Niyaz told the court that he and Chanel had stopped at True Mart to get something to eat when Chandra and her husband, Sumit, arrived and confronted them.

He alleges that both Chandra and her husband used vulgar language, while Sumit slammed the table and threatened him, saying, "I will kill you."

Niyaz says both Chandra and Chanel were filming the encounter.

He told the court that Chanel had hired him to serve a writ of summons on Chandra at her Pacific Harbour residence in June last year.

Niyaz says Chanel accompanied him to Pacific Harbour and pointed out Chandra's house from about 100 metres away.

He says he approached the residence and called out before a woman came out and asked why he was there.

Niyaz says the woman told him Chandra was inside with her children and that she would inform her of his arrival.

He says the woman later returned and asked him to wait on the verandah.

Niyaz told the court that Chandra met him about a minute later, and he explained the purpose of his visit.

He says Chandra examined the document and asked how he knew where she lived.

Niyaz alleges that Chandra then walked towards the road, swearing in Hindi, before throwing the document at the parked vehicle.

Chanel's lawyer, Kunal Singh, asked whether Chanel had entered Chandra's compound at any point or whether there had been any physical altercation, to which Niyaz said neither had occurred.

He says he then left the document at the gate before they departed.

During cross-examination, defence lawyer Mohammed Saneem asked Niyaz whether he had questioned Chanel about why the couple accused him of harassing them.

Saneem then asked whether Sumit had lunch with them, which Niyaz denied, saying Sumit had walked outside with him.

The defence lawyer also questioned whether Sumit later returned to the table to apologise.

When asked whether Sumit sat next to Chanel, Niyaz says he could not remember where Sumit sat but recalled what he ate.

Saneem then questioned whether Niyaz's appearance at Chandra's residence could have alarmed her, prompting an objection from Singh.

When asked whether he had shown any identification during the visit, Niyaz says he only presents his identification when requested.

Meanwhile, during the continuation of Chanel's cross-examination, Saneem questioned him about his responsibility as Editor and how a video he recorded ended up on social media.

Saneem asked Chanel where the buck stops, reminding him that as Editor last year, the responsibility rested with him.

He then questioned how the viral video, which Chanel recorded on his phone, ended up on the Facebook page TikTok Police and Transparency Fiji.

Chanel says he is not aware of how the video ended up on the page.

When pressed on whether he had shared the video with the page, Chanel says he had previously shared it with a few friends.

During re-examination by his lawyer Kunal Singh, Chanel clarified that they were not harassing anyone but were reporting newsworthy stories.

item.title: Ordinary ballot papers to continue being counted at polling stations in next General Election - FEO & Electoral Commission
item.description: For the upcoming General Election, the established practice of counting ordinary ballot papers at polling stations will continue. This has been stressed by the Electoral Commission and the Fijian Elections Office following concerns raised by civil society organisations regarding the recent amendments to the Electoral Act 2014, particularly the insertion of section 89A, which provides for the count
item.content:encoded:
For the upcoming General Election, the established practice of counting ordinary ballot papers at polling stations will continue.

This has been stressed by the Electoral Commission and the Fijian Elections Office following concerns raised by civil society organisations regarding the recent amendments to the Electoral Act 2014, particularly the insertion of section 89A, which provides for the counting of ballot papers at counting centres approved by the EC.

The Commission and FEO say they recognise the importance of transparency, accountability and public confidence in the electoral process and welcome constructive engagement from stakeholders on matters relating to electoral integrity.

They say Section 89A of the Electoral Act 2014, empowers the Electoral Commission to approve the counting of ballot papers at designated counting centres as an alternative to counting at polling stations while the National Referendum Act 2026 makes the equivalent provision under section 6(2), which are enabling provisions and create options for the EC.

They stress that they do not mandate a change.

The Commission and the FEO emphasize the decentralised count for ordinary ballots at polling stations remains the approach for the General Election.

They say the Commission as an independent constitutional body, is responsible for making decisions concerning electoral arrangements in accordance with the Constitution and applicable electoral legislation while the FEO, under the direction of the Supervisor of Elections, is responsible for the operational administration of elections.

They say any approval of centralised counting arrangements would involve a careful assessment of the necessary operational procedures and safeguards, including the secure handling, transportation and storage of ballot boxes, documented chain-of-custody procedures and appropriate oversight by political party polling agents and accredited observers.

The Commission and the FEO say these safeguards would be communicated clearly to all stakeholders before implementation.

They acknowledge the established counting procedures used during previous General Elections and reaffirm that the security of ballot papers, transparency of the counting process and accuracy of election results remain fundamental requirements of electoral administration, irrespective of where counting takes place.

They say centralised counting is not a new practice in Fiji's electoral process, having been implemented for postal and pre-poll ballot papers during the past three General Elections, with established procedures and safeguards in place to maintain transparency and electoral integrity.

The Commission and the FEO say they remain committed to the conduct of transparent, credible and inclusive elections and referenda in accordance with Fiji's electoral laws.

They add that they will ensure that any decisions on counting arrangements are made in the interests of electoral integrity, voter secrecy and public confidence, and that all stakeholders are kept fully informed.

item.title: One killed, four injured after gunman opens fire in Washington DC
item.description: One person has been killed and four others injured after a gunman opened fire inside a gym at an apartment building in Washington DC. Police say the suspect barricaded himself inside an apartment and fired shots at officers before being found dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
item.content:encoded:
One person has been killed and four others injured after a gunman opened fire inside a gym at an apartment building in Washington DC.

Police say the suspect barricaded himself inside an apartment and fired shots at officers before being found dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

One of the injured is in critical condition, while the other three sustained non-life-threatening injuries.

Authorities are still investigating the motive behind the shooting.

Washington DC Mayor Muriel Bowser has condemned the incident, calling it a senseless act of gun violence.

item.title: Former Fiji Ambassador to Japan Filimone Waqabaca receives Japan’s high honour for diplomatic service
item.description: Former Fiji Ambassador to Japan Filimone Waqabaca has been awarded Japan’s prestigious Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star, in recognition of his contribution to strengthening bilateral relations between Fiji and Japan. The Government of Japan announced the conferment on the 3rd of this month, as part of its 2026 Autumn Conferment of Decorations on Foreign Nationals.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Ambassador to Japan Filimone Waqabaca has been awarded Japan’s prestigious Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star, in recognition of his contribution to strengthening bilateral relations between Fiji and Japan.

The Government of Japan announced the conferment on the 3rd of this month, as part of its 2026 Autumn Conferment of Decorations on Foreign Nationals.

Waqabaca served as Fiji’s Ambassador to Japan from 2022 to 2024, where he worked with government, parliamentary, business, academic and community stakeholders to strengthen political cooperation, trade and investment, development cooperation and people-to-people exchanges.

During his tenure, he also worked to build partnerships that supported Fiji’s national interests and identified opportunities for wider regional cooperation across the Pacific.

Reflecting on the recognition, Waqabaca says his engagement with Japan had always been guided by humility, respect, patience and an appreciation of the longstanding friendship between the two countries.

He says his approach was to engage with Japan with respect, patience and a genuine understanding of its political, economic, social and cultural perspectives.

Waqabaca also expressed gratitude to the Government and people of Japan, their Imperial Majesties Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako, and the members of the Imperial Household for the friendship and support extended to him during his diplomatic service.

He acknowledged the support of his wife, Caroline, and their children, Sylvia, Silipa and Filimone Junior, as well as the Fiji Embassy team in Tokyo, former and current Fiji diplomats, and the many organisations and individuals who contributed to strengthening Fiji–Japan relations.

He also paid tribute to former First Secretary and Chargé d’Affaires a.i. Kelera Savu, whose knowledge of Japan, its culture, values and language he said played an important role in strengthening the Embassy's engagement.

Waqabaca says their work also helped advance the Lomavata Kizuna Partnership, a strategic initiative aimed at strengthening bilateral relations.

In his current roles as Chief Executive Officer of the Fiji Development Bank and Board Chair of Investment Fiji, Waqabaca continues to support Fiji's economic diplomacy, investment promotion and international business engagement.

He recently led Fiji's Trade and Investment Mission to Tokyo and Osaka, following the 2025 Fiji Business Mission held alongside Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, where he served as Commissioner General for Fiji.

Established in 1875 by Emperor Meiji, the Order of the Rising Sun was Japan's first national decoration and recognises individuals who have made distinguished contributions in areas including international relations, public service, social welfare and the promotion of Japanese culture.

The Gold and Silver Star is among the highest distinctions awarded by the Government of Japan.
